thread:
Maya Patel: quick sync — noticed a weird dip in batching utilization on prod this morning, ~72% -> ~45% over the 03:00-04:00 UTC window. token/sec also fell ~30%. anybody else see this in traces? :thinking:
Samir Chen: saw it. traces show queue depth spikes around 100-120 requests for short-window model (seq<=128). batching seems to form lots of small batches, not pooling.
Jules: I pulled a flamegraph for the runtime during the window — kernel selector started preferring the safe matmul kernel for many requests (falling back on long-seq path). that aligns with a small fraction of long prefix hits.
Ryan: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.59 concurrently. seems like more cold prefixes hit caused longer effective tokens/req. I have the KV hit histogram if useful.
Maya Patel: interesting. So a small increase in long-prefixs -> runtime picks slower kernel -> per-token latency up -> queueing breeds smaller batches -> utilization down. cascade effect.
Samir Chen: exact cascade. I also saw our continuous-batching heuristic's token_budget_target was hit very conservatively. config shows token_budget_target: 512 and max_wait_ms: 8 for the pool. that value is likely starving batches when one large request enters queue.
Jules: logging snippet from profiler (03:12 UTC):
```
[03:12:05] batcher: formed batch size=3 tokens=189 token_budget_target=512 wait_ms=9
[03:12:05] selector: model=redwood-v2 path=safe_matmul latency_ms=12.4
[03:12:05] kvcache: keys_seen=145 hit_rate=0.58
[03:12:06] gpu: active_util=56% tail_latency_ms=210
```
Ryan: also saw lots of aborted merges due to sequence-length mismatches. the batch formation policy only merges if seq variance < 32; that threshold might be too strict given the current workload skew.
Maya Patel: proposals: (1) relax seq variance threshold to 64 for this pool, (2) bump token_budget_target to 1024 for a 30-min trial, (3) add a quick KV-hit-aware bypass so if KV hit-rate drops below 0.7 we bias for larger batches.
Samir Chen: +1. I'd add a dynamic max_wait_ms increase (8 -> 16) when queue depth > 50 so we give more time for batching during transient spikes.
Jules: we should also add telemetry panels: batch_utilization (per-pool, 1m/5m), avg_batch_size, token_per_sec, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, and rejected_merge_count. Put them in Console under eng-runtime -> batching.
Maya Patel: I'll file a tiny runbook note: when batch_util < 55% and kv_hit_rate < 0.7, flip trial config; we can auto-rollback if tail latency > 250ms.
DevBot: deploy triggered by @Maya: deploy/continuous-batcher-tune -> canary on pool=short-window. changelist: token_budget_target 512 -> 1024, max_wait_ms 8 -> 16, seq_variance_threshold 32 -> 64.
InfraBot: canary rollout: 2/10 nodes active for pool=short-window. metrics collection enabled with new panels.
Ryan: running a quick microbenchmark against canary: local sim shows avg_batch_size up 1.9x, batch_util up ~20 percentage points, token/sec up 28%. no regression in 99th p50 to p99 stays stable.
Samir Chen: great. capture a perf regression watch: if kernel_fallback_rate increases > 5% we'll rollback. need alert on kernel_fallback_rate and kv_hit_rate together.
Maya Patel: agreed. Jules, can you add the dashboard widgets and an alert? put the query for kernel_fallback_rate as: `sum(rate(kernel_fallback_total[1m]))/sum(rate(requests_total[1m]))` and kv_hit_rate as `sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups)`
Jules: on it. I'll also add a small eval harness run (1000 synthetic requests, mixed seq lengths) to validate end-to-end perf and token cost. results will be attached to the thread.
Maya Patel: thanks team. we'll watch the canary for 30m, then decide. tagging @Ryan for rollback play if tail latency spikes. :thumbsup:
Ryan: standing by. will post final numbers in 30m.
Maya Patel: final note — this is a good example of cross-cutting effects: KV behavior -> kernel choice -> batching heuristics -> telemetry. we should document this causal chain in our perf playbooks.
